title: Benchmark dashboards + guardrail alerts (region health, GPU saturation, latency distributions)
author: Logan Wright
body:
Context: For the public “latency per dollar” benchmark runs we need a consistent set of dashboards + guardrail alerts that (a) verify region health during the window, (b) catch GPU saturation / throttling / thermal events that skew results, and (c) capture full latency distributions (TTFT, TPOT, end-to-end) with enough fidelity to support variance analysis and rerun decisions. This PR adds a benchmark-focused Grafana folder plus Prometheus alerting rules used by SRE during scheduled benchmark windows.

What’s included: Adds Grafana folder “Benchmark Lab” with 3 dashboards: (1) Benchmark Run Overview (templated by region, model, runner_id) showing request rate, error rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, streaming TTFT/TPOT, queueing, and retry metrics; (2) Region Health & Capacity (per region) showing API gateway health, upstream runtime health checks, instance availability, autoscaler events, and capacity headroom; (3) GPU + Node Saturation showing SM occupancy, mem bw, HBM utilization, KV cache pressure proxy, GPU memory, and node-level throttling indicators. Adds alert rules under a dedicated group benchmark_guardrails that page-on-call (SRE) for critical issues during benchmark windows and route-to-slack for warnings outside windows.

Key design points: Dashboard templating: region, model, and runner_id variables are consistent with benchmark-lab artifacts; panels use $__rate_interval and histogram_quantile() on request latency histograms (not summaries). Distribution capture: uses latency_bucket histograms for end-to-end, plus separate histograms for time_to_first_token and time_per_output_token when streaming is enabled; panels display both quantiles and heatmaps to visualize multi-modal behavior during batching changes. Guardrails: alerts focus on conditions known to invalidate a run (e.g., sustained GPU throttle, request queue growth with flat QPS, elevated 5xx, sudden latency step-change) rather than small regressions. The thresholds are aligned to the rerun policy (variance triage) and are intentionally conservative.

Alerting details: Critical pages are inhibited unless the “benchmark window” label is present to avoid noise in normal production; SRE can toggle by setting bench_window=1 on the benchmark runner and/or enabling the window override in Alertmanager (see notes below). Warnings are always emitted to Slack (#eng-sre) to catch slow drift (e.g., gradual GPU memory fragmentation / eviction storms) without paging.

Notes on labeling / data: This does not add any request payload logging. All metrics are aggregate counters/histograms and are already part of the redacted internal telemetry set. New panels only query existing metrics with standardized label keys (region, model, customer_tier=benchmark, runner_id). No customer identifiers are introduced.

Operational usage: Intended to be opened alongside the benchmark-lab orchestrator during scheduled windows; SRE uses the Overview dashboard for go/no-go and the GPU dashboard to explain variance spikes. A short runbook blurb is included in the dashboard description (linking to ENG-2895) for the escalation path.

Implementation notes: Adds a recording rule for benchmark-scoped latency quantiles so the main overview loads quickly even at high cardinality. Adds dashboard panels for “routing/fallback events” to detect unexpected regional failover during runs.

Screenshots: Not attached here (internal only); panels match the spec used in the benchmark execution checklist.

Rollout: Safe to merge; dashboards live under a new folder and alert rules are disabled by default unless bench_window=1 is present. After merge, SRE will import the folder into the shared Grafana instance and validate queries across us-east, eu-west, ap-southeast.

Checklist: [x] Dashboards use histograms (no client-side percentiles) [x] Panels scoped to benchmark tier labels [x] Alert thresholds reviewed with SRE [x] No sensitive labels added [x] CI lint for dashboards/alerts passes
commits: add(grafana): Benchmark Lab folder + overview dashboard
add(prometheus): recording rules for benchmark latency quantiles
chore: docs for bench_window labeling + alert inhibition
illustrative_snippet: Example panel query (Overview → End-to-end latency p95): histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, region, model) (rate(redwood_inference_request_latency_seconds_bucket{customer_tier="benchmark", region=~"$region", model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])))
review_conversation: Sean Gallagher: Thanks. Two asks: (1) can we add an explicit panel for autoscaler events / node churn during the run window, and (2) make sure paging alerts are inhibited outside bench windows. We had a past incident where an experimental label caused pages to fire continuously.

Logan Wright: Added a “Churn & autoscaler events” row in Region Health (scale up/down, instance terminations, node notready). For inhibition: benchmark_guardrails alerts now require bench_window="1" OR explicit override label bench_override="1" (documented).
Keiko Yamamoto: On GPU dashboard, can we include a proxy for KV cache pressure / eviction? We’ve seen TPOT spikes when eviction storms happen and occupancy alone didn’t catch it.

Logan Wright: Added panels for (a) kv_cache_evictions_total rate and (b) kv_cache_bytes_in_use / kv_cache_bytes_limit. Also added an annotation stream for “batching config changed” events if runner emits the event metric.

Caleb Johnson: Latency distributions: please avoid summaries and ensure bucket boundaries are consistent across regions. Are we using the server-side hist buckets (seconds) and not client-measured ms?

Logan Wright: Confirmed all panels use *_bucket histograms exported by the serving edge/runtime. Buckets are in seconds and consistent; no client-side ms metrics used. Added a note on the dashboard description and enforced metric name allowlist in the linter config.

Vanessa Ortiz: Capacity window usage: can we add a single “Go/No-Go” stat at top that indicates if we are within safe headroom (GPU mem < 90%, 5xx < threshold, queue stable) to help operators during the window?

Logan Wright: Added a “Run Safety” row with three big stats (Errors, Queue growth, GPU throttle) + a combined status using a recording rule. It’s conservative and intended for quick scanning; details still in panels below.
Sean Gallagher: Approving with the bench_window gating change. Please follow up after merge to validate in ap-southeast; our GPU metrics labels there sometimes differ.
Logan Wright: Will do; I’ll run a quick validation sweep post-merge and update docs if any label mapping is needed.
merge_outcome: Merged (squash) by Sean Gallagher into main
release_notes: Internal: Added Benchmark Lab dashboards and guardrail alerts for scheduled benchmark windows (region health, GPU saturation, latency distribution capture).
